# ZX80 netlist, extracted from "zx80.pdf" (ZX80 CIRCUIT DIAGRAM, redrawn by Grant Searle).
# Generated from the PDF's vector geometry + text layer, not by OCR of a raster image.
# Format: COMPONENT lines: ref | type | value.  NET lines: netname: ref.pin ref.pin ...
# Net names are the schematic's own labels; a leading / means the label is overbarred (active low).
# Auto-generated names for unlabelled nets start with _N.
# Gate packages IC11-IC20 are drawn as individual gate symbols carrying only the IC number;
#   sections are therefore identified by pin number alone, exactly as on the drawing.
# Bus connectivity (A0-A15, D0'-D7') is by label, not by wire: the fat bus lines carry no nets.
# Keyboard: each key box sits where a horizontal data rail crosses a diagonal address chain;
#   pin 1 = the rail, pin 2 = the chain. Keys are switches, open in this netlist.
# J23A/J23B are the 23-way edge connector; its pins have no drawn wires, so they join their
#   same-named nets by label. Searle's 'MALT' and 'REFSH' are read as /HALT and /RFSH.
# R31 and R33 are drawn dashed (not fitted) and have no terminals; they are omitted.
# CORRECTIONS: nets for IC16-IC21 were replaced with connectivity supplied and
#   hand-checked by the user against the schematic; they supersede the extracted values.
# VIDEO POLARITY: IC20.4 is shown on a switched connection. Normally it goes to IC9.7,
#   giving black text on a white background. The alternative position connects it to
#   IC9.9 instead, giving white text on black. This netlist wires the normal position.
# IC18.11 / 2PHI is marked uncertain by the user - verify before relying on it.
# SECOND PASS: three more corrections, user-verified against the schematic:
#   IC15.9 (the NOP-generator gate that ultimately clocks IC19's sync flip-flops)
#     is driven by /M1, not by the dangling net the first pass left it on.
#   /INT (IC1.16) is the same physical net as A6 - the Z80's own address bus
#     wired straight back into its own interrupt input, no gate in between.
#     This is the well-known "refresh counter drives the interrupt" ZX80 trick,
#     now confirmed for this schematic rather than assumed from folklore.
#   IC9.2 (the 74LS165 video shift register's CLK) is not grounded - it sits
#     between R2 (470R, to 0V) and C9 (47p, to 2PHI), the same edge-differentiator
#     pattern as the C11/R25 pair on PHI, but off the pre-divide 2PHI instead -
#     giving the shift register two shift pulses per CPU T-state (8 per M1 cycle,
#     one per pixel of a character cell).
#

## DIAGNOSTICS (read before trusting a net)
# Pins inferred from the package pinout because the drawing omits the number:
#   IC18 pin 10 - PR/CLR unnumbered on drawing
#   IC18 pin 13 - PR/CLR unnumbered on drawing
# Nets that collected more than one label. In every case checked these are stray labels
# picked up by the power-symbol rule, not merged nets - but verify before relying on them:
#   net 0V also saw: {'/KBD': 1, '0V': 4}
#   net 5V also saw: {'5V': 3, '0V': 1}
# Nets with only one pin attached (likely a label the extractor failed to read):
#   /SYNC 9V _N001 _N002 _N003 _N011 _N012 _N013 _N027 _N048
#   _N059 _N062 _N068 _N074
# Corrections applied to 46 pins; 16 of them changed the extracted net.
# Extracted nets that disagreed with the corrections and were overridden:
#   IC16.4 / IC16.5 - the two pin numbers were swapped by the extractor
#   IC16.11 - extractor had it on VIDEO; it is an input driven by /MREQ
#   IC20.12 - extractor had it with IC11.3/IC12.2; it is on the crystal node
#   the overbarred SYNC label was read onto the IC19.5 (Q) net; it belongs to IC19.6 (/Q).
#   R32 and R35 stay on SYNC, where the wiring puts them - worth a second look.
# IC21: the only connected pins are 1,2,3,5,8,9,10,11 (confirmed by the user). An
#   unnumbered line touching the box corner was a stray, not a pin, and is dropped.
